newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&Ps end sharply higher in light volume.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&Ps end sharply higher in light volume.

text.p: U.S. June Standard & Poor's 500 futures closed near record highs, but the broad-based cash market rally failed to increase floor volume, traders said.
Most futures traders tempered comments about the strength of the market's rally with the fact that volume was lighter than average in the stock index futures pits.
June S&Ps rose to 844.20 amid spotty dealer buying in the afternoon.
The contract continued its upward trend after bond futures closed for the day at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, and set the stage for a test of the major resistance area of 850.00 to 855.00.

June surpassed its previous all-time high of 838.40 around midday, but initially found profit-taking at 838.70. Once the contract re-tested 838.70, buy-stop orders took prices beyond trendline resistance at 839.25.
Some floor sources said the rally was based on mid-month portfolio re-balancing, coupled with expiration-related buying. CME May options on stock index futures expire on Friday.
However, traders said a heavy lineup of U.S. economic reports this week kept many locals on the sidelines.
Many locals and professional traders had been bracing for declines ahead of the data, which could solidfy expectations the Federal Reserve will raise rates.
"A lot of people were expecting too much on the downside ahead of that data," one institutional broker said.

The schedule of data will start with the U.S. April retail sales data at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Tuesday. Sales are forecast to fall 0.3 percent, compared to March's gain of 0.1 percent, while sales excluding automobiles are expected to rise 0.1 percent, against up 0.5 percent in March.
Some analysts have argued that the Fed will raise rates regardless of the data due to the resiliency of the bullish trend in the U.S. stock market.
"The record strength in stocks puts pressure on Greenspan to slow that down," one analyst said.

June S&Ps ended near fair value at 3.35 points. The contract traded well above fair value on Monday morning. Arbitrage buy programs are seen at a premium of 4.50 points, and arbitrage sell programs are 2.70 over.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were 11.70 higher at 841.35, Nikkei futures were up 620 at 20,280, KCBT Value Lines were up 7.05 at 735.05, NYSE Composites were up 5.90 at 437.60, Midcap 400s were up 2.50 at 271.05, Russell 2000s were up 3.40 at 365.75, and Nasdaq 100s were up 4.50 at 930.25.
